beats.text: In the US, Starbucks cards don't expire. Its latest annual report still counts $222.4 million of card money as sales, and no drink was served for it.
The reason is a forecast. From years of card data, Starbucks estimates how much money will never be redeemed.
It doesn't take that money from anyone. It books it slowly, in step with the cards people do spend.
Its filing also says part may go to government agencies under unclaimed property laws.
So who keeps the money? The store keeps the share it predicted you'd never spend. The rest is still yours.
